title: The Hardest Notes to Find on the Guitar Fretboard
excerpt: I looked at every answer Gitori players have given in the fretboard note game to find which notes are hardest to find on the guitar neck, with a live heatmap built from the real data.
content_html:
Back

Guitar

* Get it? get the joke?

Gitori's Find the Notes game challenges users to find a given note in a highlighted area of the fretboard. Over the last 3 years, the game has been played by over 10,000 people, and I've collected 275,169 different data points on note identification. Based on that data, I have a heatmap of the hardest notes to identify on the fretboard. Reds are the hardest and greens are the easiest.

Summary of findings

  1. The upper middle of the neck is hardest. The G string at frets 6 to 9 is the red zone, with the B and D strings at frets 7 to 9 close behind. The single worst spot, the G string at fret 8 (E♭), is answered incorrectly about one-third of the time.
  1. The edges are easiest. The low E string is the easiest string, then the high E. Open strings and the 12th fret are missed about 6% of the time, against roughly 20% around frets 8 and 9.
  1. Sharps and flats are harder. What a shocker! 😜 About 16% of answers on accidentals are wrong, against 12% on natural notes, and even the correct ones take about 11% longer to find (roughly 2.5 seconds against 2.2). F♯, B♭, A♭ and E♭ are the hardest note names; E is the easiest.
